title: What If Humans Were Ten Feet Tall? Your Bones Would Say No

scenes.text: What if every human grew to ten feet tall? Your bones would be the first problem.
Scale a six-foot person up to ten feet, and weight grows with volume. You'd be nearly five times heavier.
But bone strength grows only with cross-section, about two and three quarter times. Each bone carries roughly 1.7 times the load.
The tallest documented human, Robert Wadlow, reached eight feet eleven. He needed leg braces to walk and had little feeling in his legs and feet.
In 1940, a faulty brace caused an ankle infection, and he died at twenty-two.
That's the square-cube law. An elephant's bones are far thicker than a mouse's, so a ten-foot human couldn't just be us, scaled up.
